verdicts.strongest_argument: The hunter's own corroborating document refutes the claim, and I read it in the admissible window. docs/9da54838be70866b1935a4bc20f1299650419c48.txt (fetched 2026-09-02T15:08:22Z, inside clean-view's allowed snapshot 20260902T150821Z) is four Stocktwits messages, and three of them say exactly what the finding says nobody has connected: 'Should get a forward statement on their purchase of the Honeywell (PSS) business BRC purchased. This could possibly rerate this company and move higher than previous high' (09-02T14:27), 'their forward looking statements will be more valuable than actual earnings numbers considering the sale of honeywells pss business purchase that closed in August' (09-02T14:40), and 'Curious especially about forward looking with this new addition' (09-01T23:50). The specific asymmetry - that the first FY27 guide consolidating the acquisition is the event, not the quarter - is therefore in the captured pre-print stream, dated, from multiple participants, and framed bullishly. On top of that, the deal itself is in filings.json as an 8-K carrying items 1.01/2.01/2.03 on 2026-08-06, so signing, closing and the new debt were all public four weeks ahead, and a first-guide-after-a-close is a scheduled, structural event: age is not novelty. Two corrections to the record. First, the finding says the scale of the deal is 'described in docs/9da54838...' and it is not - that document contains no revenue, no purchase price and no size figure of any kind, so the assertion that the acquired business is 'roughly the acquirer's own size' has no support anywhere in this capture and the magnitude of the step-change is unestablished. Second, 'no published FY27 estimate includes the business' is inferred from n_queries=0, which measures the capture's query budget, not what the sell side had.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Pre-print retail commentary naming the Honeywell PSS purchase and predicting the forward guidance rather than the quarter will rerate the stock.
The definitive agreement, completed acquisition and new indebtedness were disclosed on EDGAR four weeks before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Admissible bars only (clean-view excludes 2026-09-03): baseline last_close 2026-09-02 at 90.18, run_up_20d -8.08%, run_up_5d -4.16%, pct_from_52w_high -8.2%, realised_vol_20d 19.5%. The -8.2% drift since completion is in the baseline's run-up field, so the deal's post-close derating is already the level. Note also that the finding's 'if the market had marked the deal to a new earnings base it would not be trading below the completion close' is a run-up inference of exactly the kind that is not admissible here - a 19.5%-vol industrial can drift 8% on rates and sector rotation without saying anything about deal accretion.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print consensus FY27 revenue or EPS figure in the capture that visibly excludes the acquired business, which would turn the step-change from an assertion into a measurable gap.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the price series describing itself, and the hunter supplies its own refutation. 454,000 shares against a 185,865 average is a fact computed from quote.json - the file every participant sees as a chart - not information withheld from the market, and the close at the bottom of a three-week range is likewise the price rather than a fact about the price. The explanation is almost certainly the mundane one the finding names and then sets aside: four Form 4s were filed the same session and Brady's fiscal year ends 31 July, so early September is precisely when annual equity grants, restricted-share settlements and the resulting sell-to-cover flow land. A 2.4x day in a 186k-share name is roughly 270k incremental shares, about 0.05% of a $4.4bn market cap - too small to be a positioning build by anyone who matters and too well explained by grant mechanics to read as directional. The independence field concedes this shares its source cluster with #0, so it adds no second observation. I stop short of 85 only because I cannot open the Form 4 bodies to confirm the grants, so a residual chance remains that the volume was something else.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Four insider transaction reports were filed on the same session as the volume spike, immediately after a 31 July fiscal year end.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json within the admissible window (bars strictly before 2026-09-03): 2026-09-02 volume 454,000 versus avg_volume_20d 185,865, close 90.18 with run_up_5d -4.16%. The incremental ~270k shares is about 0.05% of market cap. Realised_vol_20d of 19.5% and a 6.19% median historical reaction mean the print's own expected move dwarfs anything this bar implies.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Form 4 bodies showing open-market purchases or sales rather than grant and vesting codes, at a size comparable to the 454k bar.

interactions: Both findings rest on the same two objects - quote.json and filings.json - and #1 says so. More importantly, docs/9da54838be70866b1935a4bc20f1299650419c48.txt is cited by #0 as independent corroboration and is the single document that most undermines it, because it shows the guidance-reset thesis being discussed pre-print rather than missed. The same document is also miscited as the source of the deal's scale, which it does not contain.
corpus_limits: I honoured clean-view/BRC.json: I used only the six allowed snapshots and no bar dated 2026-09-03, since this is a bmo print and the event-day close is the reaction. BRC carries no news items, so there is no sell-side preview or consensus estimate - that absence is a capture artefact and I have not treated it as evidence the market lacked estimates.
